title: Statistical Inference–II
text:
CCS University, Meerut 4 credits · 60 lectures 60 lecture decks
The course gives a unified treatment of statistical decision theory, sequential procedures and distribution-free methods: how loss and risk functions provide a common framework for estimation and testing, how the sample size can be decided sequentially through an SPRT, and how valid inference can be made when no fully specified parametric model is available.

title: Statistical Inference–II
text:
Syllabus








Unit
Topics
Lectures




I
Decision theory: loss and risk functions; randomised and non-randomised decision rules; admissibility; complete, essentially complete and minimal complete classes; Bayes and minimax decision rules; estimation and testing viewed as decision problems; Bayes and minimax estimators; Bayes and minimax tests in simple cases.
20


II–III
Sequential analysis: SPRT and its applications to binomial, Poisson, normal, exponential and gamma populations; O.C. and A.S.N. functions; termination of the SPRT with probability one; Wald’s fundamental identity and its applications.
20


IV–V
Nonparametric inference: probability integral transformation; estimation of quantiles and distribution-free confidence intervals for population quantiles; tests for randomness; runs and sign tests (one and two samples); median test; Wilcoxon and Mann–Whitney tests; one- and two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests.
20

title: Research
text: My research develops classical and Bayesian methods for lifetime data, with a focus on situations where complete data are not available because of censoring. Most of this work is done with my PhD students and collaborators; the full list is on the Publications page.

title: Research
text:
Censored data and censoring schemes
Life tests are often stopped before every unit has failed, to save time and cost, and in medical studies patients may leave before the event of interest is observed. I study estimation and prediction under many censoring schemes: progressive Type-II, progressive first-failure, hybrid and unified hybrid, adaptive progressive and adaptive progressive hybrid, joint and balanced joint progressive censoring for two populations, block progressive censoring, and random censoring (including block random and progressive random censoring).

Selected papers

Krishna, H., Nagar, K., and Kumar, K. (2026). Reliability estimation in generalized inverted exponential distribution under block progressive Type-II censoring scheme. Hacettepe Journal of Mathematics and Statistics. DOI
Goel, R., Kumar, K., Ng, H. K. T., and Kumar, I. (2024). Statistical inference in Burr Type XII lifetime model based on progressive randomly censored data. Quality Engineering.
Krishna, H., Vivekanand, and Kumar, K. (2015). Estimation in Maxwell distribution with randomly censored data. Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation. DOI
Krishna, H., and Kumar, K. (2011). Reliability estimation in Lindley distribution with progressively Type-II right censored sample. Mathematics and Computers in Simulation. DOI

title: Research
text:
Stress-strength reliability
Inference for \(R = P(Y < X)\), the probability that a component’s strength \(X\) exceeds the stress \(Y\) applied to it, and for multicomponent stress-strength systems, in which a system works when at least \(s\) of its \(k\) components withstand the common stress.

Selected papers

Kumar, K., Kumari, A., and Ghosh, I. (2025). Estimation of system reliability based on inverted exponentiated Pareto distribution under a progressively first-failure censored scheme with application. Quality and Reliability Engineering International. DOI
Kumari, A., Ghosh, I., and Kumar, K. (2024). Bayesian and likelihood estimation of multicomponent stress-strength reliability from power Lindley distribution based on progressively censored samples. Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation. DOI
Kumari, A., Kumar, S., and Kumar, K. (2023). Inference for reliability in a multicomponent stress-strength model from generalized inverted exponential lifetime distribution under progressive first failure censoring. Journal of Statistical Computation and Simulation. DOI
Kumar, K., Krishna, H., and Garg, R. (2015). Estimation of \(P(Y<X)\) in Lindley distribution using progressively first failure censoring. International Journal of System Assurance Engineering and Management. DOI

title: Research
text:
Bayesian inference
Bayesian estimation of parameters, reliability characteristics and entropy under different loss functions, using Markov chain Monte Carlo methods and approximation methods such as those of Lindley and Tierney–Kadane, with highest posterior density (HPD) credible intervals. Bayesian results are compared with maximum likelihood estimates and confidence intervals through simulation studies and real data.

Selected papers

Properties, estimation and applications of lifetime models, including the Lindley and power Lindley, generalized inverted exponential, inverse Pareto and inverted exponentiated Pareto, Maxwell, Nakagami, log-logistic, inverse Weibull, inverse Rayleigh, Burr Type XII, xgamma, generalized half logistic and generalized gamma distributions, and the Weibull-G family.

title: Kapil Kumar
text:
I am a Professor in the Department of Statistics, Chaudhary Charan Singh University (CCSU), Meerut, India, where I have taught since January 2024. Before joining CCSU, I was on the faculty of the Department of Statistics at the Central University of Haryana, Mahendergarh (2016–2024), serving as Head of the Department from 2022 to 2024, and earlier taught at the Department of Statistics, University of Delhi (2012–2016).
My research is on statistical inference for lifetime data, especially when the data are censored. I work on reliability and life testing, stress-strength reliability, and classical and Bayesian estimation for lifetime distributions under a wide range of censoring schemes.
I teach Bayesian inference, survival analysis, statistical inference, linear models, design of experiments, econometrics and statistical computing with R, and I supervise PhD research in reliability and censored data.

title: Econometrics
text:
CCS University, Meerut 4 credits · 60 lectures 60 lecture decks
The course covers how econometric models are built and estimated, and what to do when the assumptions of the classical linear regression model fail: generalized least squares, multicollinearity and ridge regression, heteroskedasticity, autocorrelation, instrumental variables, and the identification and estimation of simultaneous equations models.

title: Econometrics
text:
Syllabus








Unit
Topics
Lectures




I
Introduction: objective behind building econometric models, nature of econometrics, model building and role of econometrics. Generalized least squares estimation, Aitken estimator, Gauss–Markov theorem for GLSE.
15


II
Problem of multicollinearity, its implications; sources of multicollinearity; tools for handling the problem; remedies for multicollinearity; ridge regression. Heteroskedasticity, consequences and tests for it, estimation procedures under heteroskedastic disturbances, Bartlett’s test, Breusch–Pagan test and Goldfeld–Quandt test.
15


III
Autocorrelation: concept, consequences of autocorrelated disturbances, detection and solution of autocorrelation. Instrumental variable estimation.
15


IV
Simultaneous equations model, problem of identification, necessary and sufficient condition for the identifiability of parameters in a structural equation, ordinary least squares, indirect least squares, two-stage least squares and limited information maximum likelihood method.
15
